description:
On /fly, the HUD speed readout (heliocentric km/s) shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) the entire way.

Expected: The HUD speed readout must show a plausible finite numeric heliocentric speed in km/s computed via vis-viva for the actual mission's transfer ellipse, not NaN.

Acceptance criteria:
- Loading an outer-planet mission (Galileo to Jupiter, Cassini to Saturn, Voyager 2 to Neptune, New Horizons to Pluto) on /fly must show a finite numeric speed on the HUD speed readout, not 'NaN km/s'. [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid display value for a computed quantity — the app must not show NaN to the user]
- The heliocentric speed at any waypoint must be computed via vis-viva: v = sqrt(µ * (2/r - 1/a)) * conversion_factor, where a is the transfer ellipse semi-major axis derived from the actual destination's heliocentric orbit radius, not the Earth-Mars average. [repo-data: src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts:39-41 implements heliocentricSpeed(rAu, aTransferAu); src/routes/fly/+page.svelte:952 hardcodes (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2; DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a at src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts:131-144 provides the per-destination semi-major axis for every outer-planet DestinationId]
- The speed must not be NaN at any point along the transfer arc where the spacecraft is between departure and arrival. [code-invariant: NaN is a bug — the app must not show NaN to the user]

Target: src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — line 952: $derived heliocentricKms computation
